clue.text: Grandpa, I'm told, resettled on retiring

indicators.note: to resettle is to move into a new place, so the letters of the words before are placed anew

parts.note: taken as written, letters IMTOLD

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the short word for 'on' is read backwards

parts.note: RE means 'on' or 'about', as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: Someone reports that grandpa has moved house now that he has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resettled' and 'retiring' both read as part of grandpa's story of moving and stopping work, but the first shuffles letters and the second turns a word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is, informally, an elderly man, which is what this colloquial phrase describes.

clue.text: Guide sailor follows a lot

indicators.note: follows places the sailor after the 'lot' piece in the answer

parts.note: loads is an informal word for a great deal
a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman tags along behind a group of people, as if being shown the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A guiding star, by which sailors once steered, so by extension anything that guides.

clue.text: Drive to photograph instrument of torture

parts.note: to take a picture is to photograph something
the breaking wheel, on which victims were bound and beaten, is a medieval torture device

explanation.surface: An urge to snap a picture of a grim medieval device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a noun (an urge) but is the verb: to steer a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit at the steering controls of a car is to be the one driving it, an idiom.

clue.text: Dog — stray — circling English person who enunciates badly?

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: circling means the word for 'stray' goes all round the abbreviation for English

parts.note: to err is to wander or go astray

explanation.surface: A stray mongrel runs rings round an Englishman who mumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mumbles speaks indistinctly, and the question mark admits this is a loose description.

clue.text: Working out and, after removing top, showering

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the word for 'working out' loses its opening letter

parts.note: training is exercising, working out in a gym

explanation.surface: A gym-goer finishes a workout, takes off a shirt and hits the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing top' reads as undressing, but it takes the first letter T off TRAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: Showering in the weather sense: water is falling from the sky as precipitation.

clue.text: A female inappropriately dressed for this expedition?

indicators.note: dressed means the 'A female' pieces are wrapped in the garment

parts.note: this stands for the garment that would be unsuitable for a bush trip: a sari, the draped Indian dress

explanation.surface: A woman has turned up in the wrong clothes for a trip into the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A and F (female) go inside SARI, the garment that would be inappropriate dress on such a trip, so the clue is nearly all definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to watch or hunt wild animals, typically in Africa, is a kind of expedition.

clue.text: Everyone going short after business is slack, perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the shortened 'everyone' word behind the abbreviation for business

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: going short means the word for everyone loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Trade is slow, and everybody is running out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slack' looks like an adjective about business, but it is a noun: small pieces or dust of the fuel; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack is coal dust and small fragments, so it is one example of this fuel.

clue.text: Most brazen female's in distress

indicators.note: in places the contracted 'female is' inside the word for distress

parts.note: to fret is to worry or be distressed
read as 'she's', the pronoun for a female plus the contracted 'is'

explanation.surface: The cheekiest woman is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S in "female's" looks possessive, but it is the contraction of 'is', placed inside the word for distress; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impudent, so the superlative means most impertinent.

clue.text: Hereford might be in this stunning location

definitions.text: Hereford might be in this stunning location

parts.words: Hereford might be in this stunning location
parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, and animals are stunned before slaughter, so the 'stunning location' is a slaughterhouse rather than a beauty spot

explanation.surface: The English city of Hereford is praised as a beautiful place.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is an English cathedral city, but here it is the beef cattle breed; 'stunning' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where cattle are stunned and killed for meat.

clue.text: Hoist flag

definitions.meaning: a device for lifting a car or other heavy load off the ground
a small flag flown at a ship's bow showing nationality, as in the Union one

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns: a lifting device for vehicles, and a ship's national ensign flown at the bow.

clue.text: After peeled pear, feels thrilled to consume a very soft fruit

indicators.note: After puts the thrilled feeling behind the peeled pear in the answer
peeled means the skin, here the outer letters, of the word pear is removed
to consume means the word for thrilled takes in the following pieces

parts.note: to tingle is to feel a thrill of excitement
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Having peeled a pear, someone is excited to eat a squishy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very soft' sounds like ripe fruit, but it is the musical marking pianissimo; 'peeled' strips the outer letters of the pear and 'to consume' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert apples, as opposed to cookers, are a kind of fruit eaten raw.

clue.text: China welcomes guest, one showing qualities of leadership

indicators.note: welcomes means the word for friend takes the guest and the numeral inside it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
a hotel guest staying overnight is a resident
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Chinese state receives a visiting leader at a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing the qualities of a head of state, so having the bearing of a national leader.

clue.text: One making designs, a hundred in number

indicators.note: in puts the hundred inside the word for the anaesthetic

parts.note: read as 'numb-er', something that numbs: the anaesthetic ether
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A designer has a hundred among a set number of works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but numb-er, a thing that numbs, so the anaesthetic ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver cuts designs into metal or glass with acid, so this artist makes designs.

clue.text: Nutty chocolate I put in Eton mess

indicators.note: in places the 'I put' pieces inside the jumbled school name
a mess is a jumble, so the school's name is rearranged

parts.note: to set something down is to put it there

explanation.surface: Someone drops a nut chocolate into an Eton mess, the strawberry and cream pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is a British dessert of strawberries, meringue and cream, so 'mess' looks like part of its name; it is the anagram signal, with 'in' marking the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a chocolate made with hazelnuts, French for hazelnut, so a nut-flavoured sweet.

clue.text: Pictures of royal couple visiting US state

indicators.note: visiting means the couple and royal pieces go into the state abbreviation

parts.note: Ark. is the abbreviation for Arkansas
a couple is two
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Photographs of a king and queen on a tour of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings and drawings, illustrations collectively, are works of visual creation.

clue.text: Transport café: traveller holds up object of interest

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
holds means the run of letters is contained within the first three words

explanation.surface: At a lorry drivers' roadside café, a traveller holds up an interesting item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds TCAFETRA inside 'Transport café: traveller', and 'up' reverses it. A transport café is a cheap British roadside café for lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made object of historical or cultural interest, such as a museum exhibit.

clue.text: Location of pub, you say, is close by

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: an inn's site, the spot where a pub stands

explanation.surface: Asking where the pub is, and being told it is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something visible is nearby, as in 'land was close at hand', within view.

clue.text: Man swimming in a loch beginning to shiver

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement, so the letters of 'in a loch' move about
beginning to selects the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A man in a cold Scottish lake starts to shiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges IN A LOCH; 'beginning to' takes S from 'shiver'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is a male given name, so it serves as an example of a man.

clue.text: Satellite moving a lot over Scottish island, endlessly

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: hyper means overactive, always on the go

indicators.note: endlessly means the island's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A fast-orbiting satellite passing above a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperion is a moon of Saturn, a natural satellite of the planet.

clue.text: Gift already dispatched?

definitions.meaning: something given, a birthday or Christmas offering
the question mark flags the punning split

explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a thing given; split with a hyphen, the word reads as sent in advance.

clue.text: Perhaps bully boy ripped end off ornament

parts.note: tore is the past tense of tear, so ripped

indicators.note: end off means the last letter of the word for ornament is removed

parts.note: to adorn is to ornament, decorate

explanation.surface: A thug tore a decoration, breaking the tip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully boy' looks like a thug, but read it as a man who fights bulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter is a man in the ring with bulls, so 'bully boy' cheekily describes one; 'perhaps' marks the play.

clue.text: Duke having private meal

parts.note: inner means private or personal, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is having a meal in private.
explanation.definitionFit: The main evening repast of the day is a meal.

clue.text: The Birdie Song an example of these revolutionary recordings?

definitions.text: The Birdie Song an example of these

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Was a novelty pop record a revolutionary release?
explanation.walkthrough: The Birdie Song (or Birdie Dance) was a 1981 novelty hit; the clue jokes that its tune is made of bird calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeps are the small high-pitched calls of young birds, so a song for birdies is made of them.

clue.text: Proving deficient? That's what cut-off unelasticated Bermudas may be

indicators.note: cut-off means the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: Bermuda shorts with no elastic in the waistband may drop down, so they are falling knee-length trousers

explanation.surface: Is someone failing? It is what a holidaymaker's loose Bermuda shorts might do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-off' looks like a description of the trousers but trims the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to reach a required standard or amount is to be inadequate, an idiom.

clue.text: Coward hauled up in this Spanish city

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauled up means the name is pulled upward, read backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright and wit

explanation.surface: A cowardly person is dragged up into a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person but is the playwright Noel Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: León is a city in north-western Spain, capital of its province.

clue.text: Wader twice spotted near island

indicators.note: spotted near places the 'twice' piece beside the island abbreviation

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat

explanation.surface: A wading bird is seen twice close to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is Latin for twice, as in an encore or a repeated musical passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged bird with a curved bill that feeds in shallow water, so a wading bird.

clue.text: Hot beef supplier coming round mentioned principal dish

indicators.note: coming round means the animal surrounds the abbreviation for hot

parts.note: a cow is a source of beef
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: mentioned signals that the word is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: main means principal, chief

explanation.surface: A hot beef producer drops by, and the main course is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese stir-fried noodle preparation, a popular takeaway dish.

clue.text: Fighting ultimately against American support for arms?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of 'against' is taken

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: An American struggling against an arms-supply deal, or over a broken arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support for arms' suggests weapons, but it is the bandage for a broken arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling or scuffling with someone is a form of physical fighting.
